payload.public_summary: The specification is already scientifically executable with no blocking problem-class ambiguities. I advanced the session by one frontier round with no questions, recorded the stated conventions and approximation choices as defaults owned by the derivation agent, and set the candidate as ready.

specification_sections.name: purpose
specification_sections.content: Derive the optical absorption coefficient alpha as a function of photon energy hbar omega for a direct-gap semiconductor from single-particle Bloch states in the independent-particle approximation.

specification_sections.name: scientific_target
specification_sections.content: Obtain a closed-form expression for alpha(hbar omega) together with the derivation tree leading to it.

specification_sections.name: givens_and_starting_point
specification_sections.content: Start from single-particle Bloch valence and conduction states. Use Fermi's golden rule for vertical interband transitions in a direct-gap semiconductor. Use a parabolic two-band model with conduction and valence bands, reduced mass mu, band gap Eg, and a constant momentum matrix element.

specification_sections.name: notation_and_conventions
specification_sections.content: Use SI units. Express results in terms of Eg, mu, and photon energy hbar omega. Assume unpolarized light and isotropic bands, so the response is treated as a scalar absorption coefficient.

specification_sections.name: assumptions_and_regime
specification_sections.content: Include vertical interband transitions, independent particles, parabolic two-band dispersion, constant momentum matrix element, zero temperature occupations, joint density of states, and a delta-function line shape. Exclude excitons, local-field and Coulomb enhancement effects, phonon-assisted or indirect processes, free-carrier absorption, k dot p warping beyond the parabolic edge, finite lifetime or broadening, finite temperature, and many-body self-energy effects.

specification_sections.name: scope_and_non_goals
specification_sections.content: No numerics, no code, and no materials-specific DFT. The deliverable is an analytic textbook-level derivation and closed-form alpha(hbar omega), not a material-calibrated prediction.

specification_sections.name: required_output
specification_sections.content: Provide the closed-form optical absorption coefficient alpha(hbar omega) for the specified direct-gap semiconductor model and the derivation tree that produces it, at the textbook-simplest level compatible with the stated constraints.

specification_sections.name: validation_criteria
specification_sections.content: The derivation must remain within the independent-particle, direct-gap, vertical-transition model; use SI conventions; preserve the stated included and excluded physics; and end with a closed-form alpha(hbar omega) in symbolic form using Eg and mu.

specification_sections.name: agent_discretion
specification_sections.content: Any residual non-blocking convention or presentation choice not fixed by the user is owned by the derivation agent and should follow standard textbook defaults consistent with the stated simplest-first policy.

declared_defaults.title: Unit system
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly fixed SI units, and this convention is fully compatible with the requested analytic derivation.

declared_defaults.title: Matrix-element representation
declared_defaults.statement: Use the momentum-matrix-element form for the interband coupling, with a constant matrix element.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user specified a constant momentum matrix element, making the momentum-form textbook route the direct convention.

declared_defaults.title: Line shape
declared_defaults.statement: Use an ideal delta-function line shape with no phenomenological broadening.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly excluded finite lifetime and broadening and requested a delta-function line shape.

declared_defaults.title: Route to absorption coefficient
declared_defaults.statement: Derive alpha from the interband transition rate and equivalent linear-response normalization in SI, without introducing alternative dielectric-function reconstruction routes unless needed algebraically.
declared_defaults.rationale: The target is alpha(hbar omega) itself, so the most direct textbook route minimizes unnecessary convention choices.
alternatives: Route via imaginary dielectric function epsilon_2
Route via optical conductivity then conversion to alpha

declared_defaults.title: Real-part treatment
declared_defaults.statement: Do not derive a separate real part of the dielectric function unless it is required for an intermediate consistency relation; focus directly on the absorption coefficient.
declared_defaults.rationale: The requested deliverable is alpha(hbar omega), and the excluded physics plus delta-line-shape setting make a separate real-part construction unnecessary for the baseline derivation.
alternatives: Kramers-Kronig reconstruction of the real part
External model for the real part of epsilon

declared_defaults.title: Band model
declared_defaults.statement: Use the parabolic two-band conduction-plus-valence model near the direct gap edge.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly fixed the textbook parabolic two-band model and excluded warping beyond the parabolic edge.

declared_defaults.title: k dependence of matrix element
declared_defaults.statement: Treat the interband momentum matrix element as k independent.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly fixed a constant momentum matrix element.

declared_defaults.title: Occupation model
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly fixed T = 0 and excluded finite temperature.
